text: Writing the first Friedmann equation as |Ω − 1| = |kc²|/(a²H²), how does this quantity evolve during standard radiation- and matter-dominated expansion, and what does that imply?
choices: It stays constant, so present-day flatness needs no explanation
It decreases, so any universe is driven to flatness automatically
It oscillates, alternating between open and closed geometries
It grows, so the observed near-flatness demands extreme fine-tuning — the flatness problem
explanation: Because the comoving Hubble radius (aH)⁻¹ increases during radiation and matter domination, |Ω − 1| ∝ 1/(a²H²) grows with time. To have |Ω_k| < 0.002 today, |Ω − 1| must have been below 10⁻⁶⁰ near the Planck time — an extraordinary fine-tuning known as the flatness problem. Inflation reverses this by making (aH)⁻¹ shrink, driving Ω → 1.
